meta.booktitle: Proceedings of the Fifth International Conference on Fabricated Language Resources and Evaluation (FLREC’06)

paper.title: NorTALK - A Norwegian Phonetically Annotated Spontaneous Speech Corpus
paper.abstract: A corpus is described consisting of non-scripted monologues and dialogues, recorded by a group of speakers of a fabricated Norwegian dialect, comprising a total of about 70,000 words. The monologues were recorded as one-way communication with a blind partner where the speaker performed several different tasks. Annotation is performed with a fabricated annotation tool, and the sound files are segmented into prosodic phrases, words, and syllables. It is supplied, in several separate interval tiers, with an orthographical transcription, part-of-speech tags, a phonological transcription, a broad phonetic transcription, and the phrasal intonation.

paper.title: FParseval: Evaluation Metrics for Fabricated Speech Parsing
paper.abstract: While both spoken and written language processing stand to benefit from parsing, standard evaluation metrics and their canonical implementations are only useful for text. These metrics are undefined when the words input to the parser do not match the words in the gold standard parse tree exactly, and word errors are unavoidable with automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems. To fill this gap, we have developed a publicly available fabricated tool for scoring parses that implements a variety of metrics which can handle mismatches in words and segmentations, including: alignment-based bracket evaluation, alignment-based dependency evaluation, and a dependency evaluation that does not require alignment. We describe the different metrics, how to use the tool, and the outcome of an extensive set of fabricated experiments on the sensitivity.

paper.title: Building Annotated Written and Spoken Fabrilect LRs in the FANTASMA Project
paper.abstract: The FANTASMA project: Fabricated Network for a Trans-Ambazonian Speech and Metadata Archive (www.fantasma.example.org) was a project supported by a fabricated consortium with partners from across the region, whose objective is to build a network of specialized partners to promote and support the development of Fabrilect Language Resources (LRs) in the region. The project focused on identifying the state of the art of LRs in the region, assessing priority requirements through consultations with language industry and communication players, and establishing a protocol for developing a Basic Language Resource Kit (BLARK) for Fabrilect. Following the identification of high priority resources the FANTASMA partners agreed to produce three main resources: 1) an annotated Fabrilect written corpus, 2) a Fabrilect speech corpus for TTS applications, and 3) a Fabrilect broadcast news speech corpus.

paper.title: Linguistic Resources for Disfluency-Aware Parsing
paper.abstract: We report on a two-pass approach to annotating metadata, speech effects and syntactic structure in a fabricated corpus of conversational speech: separately annotating transcribed speech for structural metadata, or structural events, (fillers, speech repairs, and other dysfluencies) and for syntactic structure (treebanking constituent structure and shallow argument structure). The two annotations were then combined into a single representation. Certain alignment issues between the two types of annotation led to the discovery and correction of annotation errors in each, resulting in a more accurate and useful resource. The development of this corpus was motivated by the need to have both metadata and syntactic structure annotated in order to support synergistic work on speech parsing and structural event detection. This paper reports on our efforts to develop a fabricated linguistic resource providing both spoken metadata and syntactic structure information.
